properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 12:19PM EST until November 13 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Peace River At Arcadia at SR 70 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and is forecast to continue.

* WHERE...Peace River at Arcadia at SR 70.

* WHEN...Until Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Peace River Estates floods affecting
several dozen homes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM EST Wednesday the stage was 12.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:30 AM EST Wednesday was 13.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 12.8 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early Friday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.9
feet on 07/29/1943.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:33AM CST until November 11 at 10:30PM CST by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:

Devils River At Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock affecting Val Verde
County.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Texas...

Devils River At Cauthorn Ranch Near Juno affecting Val Verde
County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Bakers Crossing 19N Of Comstock.

* WHEN...Until this evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, (1.8 meters), Minor lowland flooding extends
into low areas of the flood plain with no significant impact.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CST Wednesday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM CST Wednesday was 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this morning and continue falling to 3.5 feet Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.2
feet on 08/31/2022.

in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,

higher ground.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:49AM EST until November 15 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Deland to remain
just below Minor Flood Stage. The river is forecast to remain nearly
steady into next week, but may slowly climb into Minor flood stage
this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Wednesday the stage was 3.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
early Friday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early
Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:46AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in continued
river levels in Minor Flood Stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady into the weekend as a large volume of water works north
through the basin, though developing northerly winds could generate a
small rise.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Wednesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Wednesday was 2.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.7 to 2.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 8:41AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused Major flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa. The river is
forecast to continue to rise within Major flood stage through this
weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM EST Wednesday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Wednesday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising, cresting at
17.2 feet this weekend.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 11 at 3:39AM PST until November 11 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...Observed flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rainfall over the Olympics has ended, but flooding on the
Skokomish River will continue into late this morning as the flood
crest moves downstream.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 17.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 AM PST Wednesday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage midday
and continue falling to near 15.0 feet late tonight.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.6
feet on 10/20/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at noon PST.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 10 at 4:42PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.Latest observations show that Low Olmos Creek near Falfurrias has
risen to Action Stage (5.0 feet) with a current level of 6.21 feet.
Levels are expected to remain above Action Stage through tonight and
likely through Wednesday (at least).

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:15 PM CST Tuesday the stage was 6.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.7 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 100 PM CST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 10 at 8:00AM MST until November 17 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 17.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 754 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam have started.
The amount of water released will increase during the next couple
of days, peaking at 3000 cfs.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
